Heat loss is integrated into the SRD calculation. 9.3.3 Long Term Capture Efficiency During the long-term steady-state testing at ENTP, ION sought to maintain the capture efficiency between 95 and 97%. Due to the fluctuating inlet CO concentrations, controlling capture 2 efficiency in a tighter range than 95 to 97% was not feasible without feed-forward control schemes. ION operators responded to changes in the inlet CO concentration by adjusting the solvent flow 2 (L/G) to maintain a relatively constant capture efficiency. From October 2024 to February 2025, ION operated for approximately 2900 hours with an average capture efficiency of 95.8%. In Figure 9-6, the area between 95 and 97% capture is shaded in light blue. It is apparent that the capture efficiency is within the range the majority of the time, with most major excursions due to plant restarts or shutdowns. The PTR-TOF also measured emissions of ammonia, formaldehyde, and acetaldehyde. Additionally, emissions were analyzed through extractive sampling performed by a third party, Montrose Environmental. The sampling point was located on the outlet of the absorber stack, so the outlet emissions measurements were inclusive of any emissions originating from the base plant. In addition to solvent emissions, the PTR-TOF also measured other hazardous air pollutants, including ammonia, formaldehyde, and acetaldehyde. As ammonia and formaldehyde can be generated in the natural gas turbine, continuous analysis on the inlet flue gas is required to determine what portion of these emissions is passed through from the inlet flue gas and what portion is generated by the capture process.
